+"""Validate and deliver only already completed R01 fits; this CLI has no fit mode."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from r01_recovery_common import read_json, sha256_file
+from r01_recovery_delivery import export_existing_fit, grade_pair
+from r01_recovery_fit import EXPECTED_PANEL_SHA256, validate_existing_fit
+
+
+def _panel_job(panel_path: Path, job_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Select one exact existing cell from the frozen panel."""
+    if sha256_file(panel_path) != EXPECTED_PANEL_SHA256:
+        raise ValueError("R01 panel differs from the frozen source panel")
+    panel = read_json(panel_path)
+    selected = [job for job in panel.get("jobs", []) if job.get("id") == job_id]
+    if len(selected) != 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"expected one frozen R01 panel job named {job_id}")
+    return selected[0]
+
+
+def _common_arguments(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
+    """Add immutable project and recovery packet paths to one command."""
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--root", type=Path, required=True, help="project root /data/epanov_s/tabdata"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--packet", type=Path, required=True, help="frozen runtime/b300-r01-v1")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--source-root", type=Path, required=True, help="frozen runtime/source-a266-lf-subset-v1"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--recovery-root",
+        type=Path,
+        required=True,
+        help="new isolated state/r01-delivery-recovery-v2 directory",
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    """Run one read-only fit validation, one fixed-endpoint export, or one paired grade."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="phase", required=True)
+    validate_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
+        "validate", help="CPU validate one existing complete fit"
+    )
+    _common_arguments(validate_parser)
+    validate_parser.add_argument("--job-id", required=True)
+    export_parser = subparsers.add_parser("export", help="export a validated existing epoch-5 fit")
+    _common_arguments(export_parser)
+    export_parser.add_argument("--job-id", required=True)
+    grade_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
+        "grade", help="officially grade one same-seed wide/deep pair"
+    )
+    _common_arguments(grade_parser)
+    grade_parser.add_argument("--wide-id", required=True)
+    grade_parser.add_argument("--deep-id", required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    panel = args.packet / "PANEL.json"
+    if args.phase == "validate":
+        result = validate_existing_fit(
+            args.root,
+            args.packet,
+            args.source_root,
+            args.recovery_root,
+            _panel_job(panel, args.job_id),
+        )
+    elif args.phase == "export":
+        _panel_job(panel, args.job_id)
+        result = export_existing_fit(
+            args.root,
+            args.packet,
+            args.source_root,
+            args.recovery_root,
+            args.job_id,
+        )
+    else:
+        _panel_job(panel, args.wide_id)
+        _panel_job(panel, args.deep_id)
+        result = grade_pair(
+            args.root,
+            args.packet,
+            args.source_root,
+            args.recovery_root,
+            args.wide_id,
+            args.deep_id,
+        )
+    print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+    verify_runtime_envelope,
+    verify_watcher_files,

+from delivery_watch_grades import _grade_pair, _publish

+
+def _load_config(path: Path, expected_sha256: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Check the root-supplied config, helper bundle, and frozen panel."""
+    if sha256_file(path) != expected_sha256:
+        raise ValueError("watcher config SHA-256 differs from the service pin")
+    config = read_object(path)
+    required = {
+        "root",
+        "helper_dir",
+        "helper_manifest_name",
+        "helper_manifest_sha256",
+        "absolute_deadline_unix",
+        "gpu_uuid",
+        "publisher_config_path",
+        "publisher_config_sha256",
+        "watcher_files",
+    }

+        config.get("schema") != "tabdata-r01-delivery-watch-config.v1"
+        or not required.issubset(config)
+        or config["helper_manifest_name"] != "MANIFEST.json"
+        or config["absolute_deadline_unix"] != EXPECTED_DEADLINE_UNIX
+        or config["helper_manifest_sha256"] != HELPER_MANIFEST_SHA256
+    ):

+    verify_watcher_files(script_dir, config["watcher_files"])
+    root = Path(config["root"]).resolve(strict=True)
+    helper = Path(config["helper_dir"]).resolve(strict=True)
+    expected_helper = (root / "runtime/r01-delivery-recovery-v2_4").resolve(strict=True)
+    if helper != expected_helper:
+        raise ValueError("helper directory differs from runtime/r01-delivery-recovery-v2_4")

+    panel_path = packet / "PANEL.json"
+    if sha256_file(panel_path) != PANEL_SHA256:
+        raise ValueError("frozen R01 panel hash differs from the reviewed panel")

+    if not isinstance(jobs, list) or len(jobs) != 60 or len({j.get("id") for j in jobs}) != 60:

+        **config,
+        "root_path": root,
+        "helper_path": helper,
+        "packet_path": packet,
+        "jobs": jobs,

+
+
+def _summary(cells: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Summarize delivery outcomes without treating fit failures as scores."""
+    fits = [c.get("fit", {}).get("status", "pending") for c in cells.values()]
+    exports = [c.get("export", {}).get("status", "pending") for c in cells.values()]
+    grades = [c.get("grade", {}).get("status", "pending") for c in cells.values()]
+    return {
+        "fit_counts": {
+            s: fits.count(s)
+            for s in ("validated", "rejected", "preserved_partial", "pending", "validation_started")
+        },
+        "export_counts": {
+            s: exports.count(s)
+            for s in (
+                "exported",
+                "rejected",
+                "preserved_partial",
+                "not_applicable",
+                "pending",
+                "export_started",
+            )
+        },
+        "fit_terminal_count": sum(
+            s in {"validated", "rejected", "preserved_partial"} for s in fits
+        ),
+        "export_terminal_count": sum(
+            s in {"exported", "rejected", "preserved_partial", "not_applicable"} for s in exports
+        ),
+        "grade_count": grades.count("graded"),
+        "grade_terminal_count": sum(
+            s in {"graded", "preserved_partial", "not_applicable"} for s in grades
+        ),
+        "scores_claimed": grades.count("graded"),
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    """Run the finite delivery monitor under its separately bounded service unit."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--config-sha256", required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    config = _load_config(args.config, args.config_sha256)
+    verify_runtime_envelope(str(config["gpu_uuid"]))
+    root, helper = config["root_path"], config["helper_path"]
+    recovery = root / "state/r01-delivery-recovery-v2"
+    if recovery.is_symlink() or not recovery.is_dir():
+        raise ValueError("recovery tree must be an existing nonsymlink directory")
+    state = root / "state/r01-delivery-watch-v2"
+    if state.is_symlink():
+        raise ValueError("watcher state cannot be a symlink")
+    state.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    import fcntl
+
+    lock = (state / "watcher.lock").open("a+")
+    try:
+        fcntl.flock(lock.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
+    except OSError as error:
+        lock.close()
+        raise RuntimeError("another delivery watcher already owns this state") from error
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(helper))
+    from r01_recovery_delivery import grade_pair
+    from r01_recovery_placement import verify_placement
+
+    delivery = sys.modules["r01_recovery_delivery"]
+    jobs = config["jobs"]
+    cells = {str(job["id"]): _cell_load(state, job) for job in jobs}
+    stable: dict[str, tuple[str, float]] = {}
+    last_publish = 0.0
+    append_event(
+        state / "events.jsonl",
+        {
+            "time_unix": time.time(),
+            "phase": "watcher_started",
+            "panel_sha256": PANEL_SHA256,
+            "deadline_unix": EXPECTED_DEADLINE_UNIX,
+        },
+    )
+    while time.time() < EXPECTED_DEADLINE_UNIX:
+        for job in jobs:
+            cell = cells[str(job["id"])]
+            if cell.get("fit", {}).get("status") in {"pending", "validation_started"}:
+                _fit_one(config, state, recovery, job, cell, stable, delivery, verify_placement)
+            if cell.get("export", {}).get("status") in {"pending", "export_started"}:
+                _export_one(config, state, recovery, job, cell, delivery, verify_placement)
+            last_publish = _publish(config, state, force=False, last_time=last_publish)
+        pairs: dict[tuple[int, int], dict[str, Any]] = {}
+        for job in jobs:
+            pairs.setdefault((int(job["fold"]), int(job["seed"])), {})[str(job["arm"])] = job
+        for (fold, seed), pair in sorted(pairs.items()):
+            if set(pair) != {"wide", "deep"}:
+                raise ValueError(f"frozen panel pair is malformed at fold {fold}, seed {seed}")
+            last_publish = _grade_pair(
+                config,
+                state,
+                recovery,
+                pair["wide"],
+                pair["deep"],
+                cells,
+                grade_pair,
+                last_publish,
+            )
+        last_publish = _publish(config, state, force=False, last_time=last_publish)
+        summary = _summary(cells)
+        write_atomic(
+            state / "STATUS.json",
+            {
+                "schema": "tabdata-r01-delivery-watch-status.v1",
+                "heartbeat_unix": time.time(),
+                "panel_sha256": PANEL_SHA256,
+                "deadline_unix": EXPECTED_DEADLINE_UNIX,
+                **summary,
+            },
+        )
+        if (
+            summary["fit_terminal_count"] == 60
+            and summary["export_terminal_count"] == 60
+            and summary["grade_terminal_count"] == 30
+        ):
+            break
+        seconds_left = max(0, int(EXPECTED_DEADLINE_UNIX - time.time()))
+        if seconds_left <= 0:
+            break
+        time.sleep(min(POLL_SECONDS, seconds_left))
+    summary = _summary(cells)
+    complete = (
+        summary["fit_counts"]["validated"] == 60
+        and summary["export_counts"]["exported"] == 60
+        and summary["grade_count"] == 30
+    )
+    write_atomic(
+        state / "RESULT.json",
+        {
+            "schema": "tabdata-r01-delivery-watch-result.v1",
+            "status": "complete" if complete else "partial",
+            "finished_unix": time.time(),
+            "panel_sha256": PANEL_SHA256,
+            **summary,
+        },
+    )
+    append_event(
+        state / "events.jsonl", {"time_unix": time.time(), "phase": "watcher_finished", **summary}
+    )
+    lock.close()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Small file and source-identity helpers for the R01 delivery recovery packet."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import re
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+PORTABLE_ONLY_FILE = "src/wnn/training/README.md"
+CHECKPOINT_IDENTITY_SHA256 = "a1ed31086f6b9154e798a363d7b44daeaa6a6128f5cc4ea86741b1a4c161e537"
+
+
+def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
+    """Hash one file in bounded memory."""
+    if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
+        raise ValueError(f"expected a regular nonsymlink file: {path}")
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as stream:
+        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(4 * 1024**2), b""):
+            digest.update(block)
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+
+
+def read_json(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Read an object-valued UTF-8 JSON receipt."""
+    if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
+        raise ValueError(f"expected a regular nonsymlink JSON file: {path}")
+    value = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    if not isinstance(value, dict):
+        raise TypeError(f"expected JSON object: {path}")
+    return value
+
+
+def write_json_new(path: Path, value: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Create a durable JSON receipt without replacing prior recovery evidence."""
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    if path.exists() or path.is_symlink():
+        raise FileExistsError(f"refusing to overwrite recovery evidence: {path}")
+    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".r01-recovery-", dir=path.parent)
+    try:
+        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
+            json.dump(value, stream, sort_keys=True, indent=2, allow_nan=False)
+            stream.write("\n")
+            stream.flush()
+            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
+        os.link(temporary, path)
+    finally:
+        if os.path.exists(temporary):
+            os.unlink(temporary)
+
+
+def require_under(path: Path, parent: Path, label: str) -> Path:
+    """Resolve an existing path and require it to remain within its declared root."""
+    resolved = path.resolve(strict=True)
+    root = parent.resolve(strict=True)
+    if resolved == root or not resolved.is_relative_to(root):
+        raise ValueError(f"{label} escapes its declared root: {resolved}")
+    return resolved
+
+
+def producer_source_identity(portable_files: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Derive the trainer's 60-file identity from the exact 61-file portable map."""
+    if PORTABLE_ONLY_FILE not in portable_files or len(portable_files) != 61:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "portable a266 identity must contain its one training README and 60 code files"
+        )
+    if any(
+        not isinstance(name, str)
+        or not isinstance(digest, str)
+        or re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", digest) is None
+        for name, digest in portable_files.items()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("portable a266 source map contains a malformed path or SHA-256")
+    producer_files = dict(portable_files)
+    producer_files.pop(PORTABLE_ONLY_FILE)
+    encoded = json.dumps(producer_files, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
+    return {
+        "schema": "wnn.training-source.v1",
+        "source_identity_sha256": hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest(),
+        "files": producer_files,
+        "portable_source_identity_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
+            json.dumps(portable_files, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
+        ).hexdigest(),
+        "portable_only_file": PORTABLE_ONLY_FILE,
+    }
+
+
+def validate_epoch_records(
+    history: list[dict[str, Any]], provenance: dict[str, Any]
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Require six full, internally consistent fit-only epoch records and counters."""
+
+    def require_finite(value: Any, label: str) -> None:
+        if isinstance(value, float) and not math.isfinite(value):
+            raise ValueError(f"{label} contains a nonfinite recorded value")
+        if isinstance(value, dict):
+            for item in value.values():
+                require_finite(item, label)
+        elif isinstance(value, list):
+            for item in value:
+                require_finite(item, label)
+
+    require_finite(history, "R01 fit history")
+    require_finite(provenance, "R01 fit provenance")
+    if len(history) != 6 or any(
+        type(row.get("epoch")) is not int or row.get("epoch") != index
+        for index, row in enumerate(history)
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("R01 recovery requires the exact six completed epoch indices 0..5")
+    if any(row.get("evaluation") != "withheld" for row in history):
+        raise ValueError("R01 history contains an outer evaluation during fitting")
+    args = provenance.get("args", {})
+    groups = provenance.get("fit_row_groups", {})
+    if args.get("batch") != 8 or args.get("chunk") != 2000:
+        raise ValueError("Full R01 budget requires its frozen batch8/chunk2000 recipe")
+    if not isinstance(groups.get("train"), list) or not isinstance(groups.get("valid"), list):
+        raise ValueError("Full R01 budget requires source-qualified fit membership")
+    expected_batches = (len(groups["train"]) + len(groups["valid"])) // 8
+    expected_updates = expected_batches * 10  # 20000 rows, ten chunk2000 optimizer windows.
+    updates: list[int] = []
+    provenance_updates = provenance.get("update_diagnostics")
+    if not isinstance(provenance_updates, list) or len(provenance_updates) != 6:
+        raise ValueError("provenance lacks six per-epoch update-count records")
+    for index, row in enumerate(history):
+        diagnostics = row.get("update_diagnostics", {})
+        epoch_counts = diagnostics.get("epoch", {})
+        expected = provenance_updates[index]
+        if (
+            not isinstance(expected, dict)
+            or type(expected.get("epoch_index")) is not int
+            or expected.get("epoch_index") != index
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("provenance update records are not in canonical epoch order")
+        recorded_counts = expected.get("epoch", {})
+        if not isinstance(recorded_counts, dict):
+            raise ValueError("provenance epoch counter is malformed")
+        keys = (
+            "optimizer_attempts",
+            "optimizer_completed_updates",
+            "amp_skipped_updates",
+            "completed_batches",
+        )
+        if any(type(epoch_counts.get(key)) is not int for key in keys):
+            raise ValueError("history lacks exact integer optimizer/batch counters")
+        if any(epoch_counts.get(key) != recorded_counts.get(key) for key in keys):
+            raise ValueError("history and provenance disagree on epoch update counts")
+        attempts = epoch_counts["optimizer_attempts"]
+        if (
+            attempts <= 0
+            or attempts != expected_updates
+            or epoch_counts["optimizer_completed_updates"] != attempts
+            or epoch_counts["amp_skipped_updates"] != 0
+            or epoch_counts["completed_batches"] != expected_batches
+            or type(row.get("fit_summary", {}).get("optimizer_windows")) is not int
+            or row["fit_summary"]["optimizer_windows"] != attempts
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "an epoch is partial, skipped updates, or has inconsistent batch counts"
+            )
+        updates.append(attempts)
+    if len(set(updates)) != 1:
+        raise ValueError("full R01 epochs do not have the same canonical update budget")
+    cumulative = provenance.get("cumulative_updates", {})
+    cumulative_keys = (
+        "optimizer_attempts",
+        "optimizer_completed_updates",
+        "amp_skipped_updates",
+        "completed_batches",
+    )
+    if any(type(cumulative.get(key)) is not int for key in cumulative_keys) or any(
+        cumulative.get(key) != sum(row["update_diagnostics"]["epoch"][key] for row in history)
+        for key in cumulative_keys
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("provenance cumulative optimizer counts differ from the six epochs")
+    return {"per_epoch": updates[0], "total": sum(updates), "epochs": 6}

+) -> tuple[Path, dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Load a successful fit-recovery receipt and verify its separate fit view."""
+    panel_path = packet_root / "PANEL.json"
+    if sha256_file(panel_path) != EXPECTED_PANEL_SHA256:
+        raise ValueError("R01 panel differs from the frozen source panel")
+    panel = read_json(panel_path)
+    matches = [job for job in panel.get("jobs", []) if job.get("id") == job_id]
+    if len(matches) != 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"job is not present exactly once in the frozen R01 panel: {job_id}")
+    if recovery_root.is_symlink():
+        raise ValueError("recovery root cannot be a symlink")
+    recovery_root = recovery_root.resolve(strict=True)
+    path = recovery_root / "receipts" / f"{job_id}.json"
+    if path.is_symlink():
+        raise ValueError("fit recovery receipt cannot be a symlink")
+    receipt = read_json(path)

+        raise ValueError("recovery fit view cannot itself be a symlink")

+        receipt.get("schema") != "tabdata-r01-fit-recovery.v2"
+        or receipt.get("status") != "existing_fit_validated_no_refit"
+        or receipt.get("job", {}).get("id") != job_id
+        or receipt.get("job") != matches[0]
+        or view != recovery_root.resolve(strict=True) / "fit_views" / job_id
+        or not (view / "producer_receipt.json").is_file()
+        or (view / "producer_receipt.json").is_symlink()
+        or sha256_file(view / "producer_receipt.json") != receipt.get("recovery_fit_receipt_sha256")

+
+def export_existing_fit(

+    if not visible_devices.startswith("GPU-") or "," in visible_devices:

+    output = recovery_root / "exports" / job_id

+    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

+        sys.executable,

+        recovery["fit_view"],
+        "--export-dir",
+        str(output),

+        "--seed",
+        str(job["seed"]),

+    ]

+    actor_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    env = dict(
+        os.environ,
+        CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=visible_devices,
+        WNN_RUN_DIR=str(output),
+        PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1",
+    )
+    with actor_log.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as log:
+        process = subprocess.run(
+            argv,

+        or type(resource.get("cuda_peak_reserved_bytes")) is not int

+    if saved_receipt != command_receipt or saved_receipt.get("fit_receipt_sha256") != sha256_file(
+        Path(recovery["fit_view"]) / "producer_receipt.json"
+    ):

+    recovery_export = {
+        "schema": "tabdata-r01-export-recovery.v2",
+        "status": "exported_fixed_epoch5_no_refit",
+        "job_id": job_id,

+def _load_module(name: str, path: Path) -> Any:
+    """Load one exact local module by path for isolated recovery checks."""
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
+    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
+        raise ImportError(f"cannot load {name} from {path}")
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules[name] = module
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module

+"""Bind changed R01 CPU placement to the already sealed density successor."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from r01_recovery_common import read_json, sha256_file
+
+DENSITY_MANIFEST_SHA256 = "e9927b5970c630b24284b4bc6d0fe5788f23546daa1755859f39573f6a4bcb6f"
+
+
+def verify_placement(
+    project_root: Path, job: dict[str, Any], resource: dict[str, Any]
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Accept initial placement or an exact PID/argv-bound successor launch event."""
+    if resource.get("visible_devices") != job.get("gpu_uuid"):
+        raise ValueError("R01 fit moved away from its panel GPU")
+    if resource.get("cpu_affinity") == job.get("cpu_ids_initial"):
+        return {"authority": "frozen_panel_initial_placement"}
+    control = project_root / "runtime/r01-density4-v1"
+    manifest_path = control / "CONTROL_MANIFEST.json"
+    if sha256_file(manifest_path) != DENSITY_MANIFEST_SHA256:
+        raise ValueError("changed placement requires the exact density4 control manifest")
+    manifest = read_json(manifest_path)
+    files = manifest.get("files")
+    if (
+        manifest.get("schema") != "tabdata-r01-density4-control-bundle.v1"
+        or not isinstance(files, dict)
+        or not files
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("density4 control manifest is malformed")
+    for name, digest in files.items():
+        if Path(name).name != name or not name.endswith(".py"):
+            raise ValueError("unsafe density4 control member")
+        if sha256_file(control / name) != digest:
+            raise ValueError(f"changed density4 control member: {name}")
+    canonical = json.dumps(files, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
+    if manifest.get("sha256") != hashlib.sha256(canonical).hexdigest() or {
+        path.name for path in control.glob("*.py")
+    } != set(files):
+        raise ValueError("density4 control member set/identity differs")
+    events_path = project_root / "state/r01-density4-v1/events.jsonl"
+    if events_path.is_symlink() or not events_path.is_file():
+        raise ValueError("density4 launch evidence is not a regular event log")
+    matches = []
+    with events_path.open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
+        for line in stream:
+            # A concurrently appended final partial line is not durable evidence.
+            if not line.endswith("\n"):
+                continue
+            event = json.loads(line)
+            if event.get("event") == "fit_started" and event.get("job_id") == job.get("id"):
+                matches.append(event)
+    if len(matches) != 1:
+        raise ValueError("changed placement needs exactly one durable density4 launch")
+    event = matches[0]
+    argv_sha = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(job["argv"], separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()
+    cpus, pid = resource.get("cpu_affinity"), resource.get("pid")
+    if (
+        type(pid) is not int
+        or pid <= 0
+        or not isinstance(cpus, list)
+        or len(cpus) != 2
+        or any(type(cpu) is not int or cpu < 0 for cpu in cpus)
+        or len(set(cpus)) != 2
+        or any(event.get(key) != job.get(key) for key in ("arm", "fold", "seed"))
+        or event.get("pid") != pid
+        or event.get("pgid") != pid
+        or type(event.get("pid_start_ticks")) is not int
+        or event["pid_start_ticks"] <= 0
+        or event.get("cpu_ids") != cpus
+        or event.get("gpu_uuid") != resource.get("visible_devices")
+        or event.get("argv_sha256") != argv_sha
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("density4 launch does not bind the actual resource/PID/panel argv")
+    encoded = json.dumps(event, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
+    return {
+        "authority": "sealed_density4_launch_event",
+        "control_manifest_path": str(manifest_path),
+        "control_manifest_sha256": DENSITY_MANIFEST_SHA256,
+        "event_log_path": str(events_path),
+        "launch_event": event,
+        "launch_event_sha256": hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest(),
+        "panel_initial_cpu_ids": job["cpu_ids_initial"],
+        "actual_cpu_ids": cpus,
+    }

+def _complete_history(*, skipped_epoch: int | None = None) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]:
+    """Build minimal valid six-epoch counter records for pure invariants."""
+    history = []
+    provenance_rows = []
+    for epoch in range(6):
+        skipped = int(epoch == skipped_epoch)
+        counts = {
+            "optimizer_attempts": 10,
+            "optimizer_completed_updates": 10 - skipped,
+            "amp_skipped_updates": skipped,
+            "completed_batches": 1,
+        }
+        history.append(
+            {
+                "epoch": epoch,
+                "evaluation": "withheld",
+                "update_diagnostics": {"epoch": counts},
+                "fit_summary": {"optimizer_windows": 10},
+            }
+        )
+        provenance_rows.append({"epoch_index": epoch, "epoch": counts})
+    provenance = {
+        "args": {"batch": 8, "chunk": 2000},
+        "fit_row_groups": {"train": list(range(7)), "valid": [0]},
+        "update_diagnostics": provenance_rows,
+        "cumulative_updates": {
+            "optimizer_attempts": 60,
+            "optimizer_completed_updates": sum(
+                row["update_diagnostics"]["epoch"]["optimizer_completed_updates"] for row in history
+            ),
+            "amp_skipped_updates": int(skipped_epoch is not None),
+            "completed_batches": 6,
+        },
+    }
+    return history, provenance
+
+
+class EpochBudgetTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Reject incomplete, skipped or internally inconsistent fit histories."""
+
+    def test_accepts_six_complete_fit_epochs(self) -> None:
+        history, provenance = _complete_history()
+        self.assertEqual(
+            validate_epoch_records(history, provenance), {"per_epoch": 10, "total": 60, "epochs": 6}
+        )
+
+    def test_rejects_amp_skip_even_when_history_is_six_epochs(self) -> None:
+        history, provenance = _complete_history(skipped_epoch=3)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            validate_epoch_records(history, provenance)
+
+    def test_actual_fold0_counter_scope_has_ten_updates_per_completed_batch(self) -> None:
+        history, provenance = _complete_history()
+        provenance["fit_row_groups"] = {"train": list(range(10535)), "valid": list(range(1405))}
+        for epoch, row in enumerate(history):
+            counts = {
+                "optimizer_attempts": 14920,
+                "optimizer_completed_updates": 14920,
+                "amp_skipped_updates": 0,
+                "completed_batches": 1492,
+            }
+            row["update_diagnostics"]["epoch"] = counts
+            row["fit_summary"]["optimizer_windows"] = 14920
+            provenance["update_diagnostics"][epoch]["epoch"] = counts
+        provenance["cumulative_updates"] = {
+            "optimizer_attempts": 89520,
+            "optimizer_completed_updates": 89520,
+            "amp_skipped_updates": 0,
+            "completed_batches": 8952,
+        }
+        self.assertEqual(validate_epoch_records(history, provenance)["total"], 89520)
+        history[0]["update_diagnostics"]["epoch"]["completed_batches"] = 14920
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            validate_epoch_records(history, provenance)
+
+    def test_rejects_missing_or_evaluated_epoch(self) -> None:
+        history, provenance = _complete_history()
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            validate_epoch_records(history[:-1], provenance)
+        history[2]["evaluation"] = {"wp": 0.01}
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            validate_epoch_records(history, provenance)
+        history[2]["fit_summary"]["loss"] = float("nan")
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            validate_epoch_records(history, provenance)

+if __name__ == "__main__":

+"""Validate epoch-zero smoke artifacts with pinned checkpoint and grader code."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib
+import importlib.util
+import inspect
+import json
+import math
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from feature_common import ARMS, GRADER_SHA256, read, sha  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def set_option(argv: list[str], flag: str, value: str) -> None:
+    """Replace one recipe option while rejecting ambiguous command lines."""
+    positions = [index for index, item in enumerate(argv) if item == flag]
+    if len(positions) != 1 or positions[0] + 1 >= len(argv):
+        raise ValueError(f"canonical recipe must contain exactly one value for {flag}")
+    argv[positions[0] + 1] = value
+
+
+def options(argv: list[str]) -> dict[str, str | bool]:
+    """Parse the small canonical command surface needed by the smoke contract."""
+    parsed: dict[str, str | bool] = {}
+    index = 0
+    while index < len(argv):
+        token = argv[index]
+        if not token.startswith("--"):
+            index += 1
+            continue
+        key = token[2:]
+        if key in parsed:
+            raise ValueError(f"canonical argv repeats --{key}")
+        if index + 1 < len(argv) and not argv[index + 1].startswith("--"):
+            parsed[key] = argv[index + 1]
+            index += 2
+        else:
+            parsed[key] = True
+            index += 1
+    return parsed
+
+
+def load_grader(root: Path, source: Path) -> Any:
+    """Load the official scorer after prioritizing the pinned trainer source."""
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(source / "src"))
+    for name in ("wnn.data", "wnn.evaluation", "wnn.gmetric", "wnn.splits"):
+        importlib.import_module(name)
+    path = root / "runtime/b300-r01-v1/grader/grade_endpoint.py"
+    if path.is_symlink() or sha(path) != GRADER_SHA256:
+        raise ValueError("official grader differs from its frozen source hash")
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("_smoke_official_grader", path)
+    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
+        raise ImportError("cannot load pinned official endpoint grader")
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules[spec.name] = module
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+def _finite_tree(value: Any, label: str) -> None:
+    """Reject nonfinite numeric values in saved training evidence."""
+    if isinstance(value, float) and not math.isfinite(value):
+        raise ValueError(f"nonfinite training evidence at {label}")
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        for key, child in value.items():
+            _finite_tree(child, f"{label}.{key}")
+    elif isinstance(value, list):
+        for index, child in enumerate(value):
+            _finite_tree(child, f"{label}[{index}]")
+
+
+def validate_fit(
+    work: Path, job: dict[str, Any], subset: dict[str, Any], split_sha: str, legacy: dict
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Check one withheld epoch, exact fit membership, gradient counts and FP32 state."""
+    import torch
+
+    run_dir = work / "artifacts/runs" / job["id"]
+    paths = {
+        name: run_dir / name
+        for name in (
+            "model_ep0.pt",
+            "model.pt",
+            "training_state.pt",
+            "history.json",
+            "provenance.json",
+        )
+    }
+    if any(path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file() for path in paths.values()):
+        raise FileNotFoundError("trainer omitted an expected epoch-zero smoke artifact")
+    provenance = read(paths["provenance.json"])
+    history = json.loads(paths["history.json"].read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    if (
+        not isinstance(history, list)
+        or len(history) != 1
+        or history[0].get("epoch") != 0
+        or history[0].get("evaluation") != "withheld"
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("smoke fit must contain one evaluation-withheld epoch zero")
+    args = provenance.get("args")
+    feature, control, width = ARMS[job["arm"]][1:]
+    expected = {
+        "name": job["id"],
+        "valid_fold": 0,
+        "seed": job["seed"],
+        "hidden": 16,
+        "layers": 1,
+        "epochs": 1,
+        "checkpoint_policy": "fixed",
+        "checkpoint_epoch": 0,
+        "precision": "fp32",
+        "device": "cuda",
+        "research_features": feature,
+        "research_feature_control": control,
+        "batch": 2,
+        "chunk": 2000,
+        "train_source": "train+valid",
+        "train_seqs": 10607,
+        "valid_train_fraction": 1.0,
+        "valid_repeat": 1,
+        "no_eval_during_fit": True,
+        "save_training_state": True,
+        "fit_subset_manifest_sha256": subset["sha256"],
+    }
+    if not isinstance(args, dict) or any(args.get(key) != value for key, value in expected.items()):
+        raise ValueError("saved trainer arguments differ from the engineering smoke contract")
+    if (
+        provenance.get("split_manifest_sha256") != split_sha
+        or provenance.get("fit_subset_manifest_sha256") != subset["sha256"]
+        or provenance.get("fit_subset_members_sha256") != subset["selected_members_sha256"]
+        or provenance.get("selected_epoch") != 0
+        or provenance.get("fit_row_groups") != subset["selected_groups"]
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("fit provenance does not bind the frozen split, subset and endpoint")
+    update_diagnostics = history[0].get("update_diagnostics")
+    diagnostics = update_diagnostics.get("epoch") if isinstance(update_diagnostics, dict) else None
+    if not isinstance(diagnostics, dict):
+        raise ValueError("history lacks per-epoch optimizer counters")
+    attempts = diagnostics.get("optimizer_attempts")
+    completed = diagnostics.get("optimizer_completed_updates")
+    skipped = diagnostics.get("amp_skipped_updates")
+    grad = update_diagnostics.get("grad_stats")
+    if (
+        type(attempts) is not int
+        or attempts <= 0
+        or completed != attempts
+        or skipped != 0
+        or not isinstance(grad, dict)
+        or grad.get("steps") != attempts
+        or grad.get("nonfinite_steps") != 0
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("optimizer or pre-clip gradient counts are incomplete/nonfinite")
+    _finite_tree(history, "history")
+    _finite_tree(provenance, "provenance")
+    identity = legacy["checkpoint_identity"].verify_checkpoint_pair(
+        paths["model_ep0.pt"], paths["model.pt"], expected_epoch=0, expected_input_width=width
+    )
+    checkpoint = torch.load(paths["model_ep0.pt"], map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
+    embedded = checkpoint.get("provenance")
+    recorded = provenance.get("checkpoint_sha256")
+    if (
+        checkpoint.get("args") != args
+        or not isinstance(embedded, dict)
+        or embedded.get("args") != args
+        or embedded.get("split_manifest_sha256") != split_sha
+        or embedded.get("fit_subset_manifest_sha256") != subset["sha256"]
+        or embedded.get("fit_subset_members_sha256") != subset["selected_members_sha256"]
+        or embedded.get("fit_row_groups") != subset["selected_groups"]
+        or not isinstance(recorded, dict)
+        or recorded.get("model_ep0.pt") != identity.fixed_file_sha256
+        or recorded.get("model.pt") != identity.selected_file_sha256
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint, run provenance and file digests disagree")
+    shapes = {
+        "mean": (width,),
+        "std": (width,),
+        "inp.weight": (16, width),
+        "inp.bias": (16,),
+        "gru.weight_ih_l0": (48, 16),
+        "gru.weight_hh_l0": (48, 16),
+        "gru.bias_ih_l0": (48,),
+        "gru.bias_hh_l0": (48,),
+        "head.0.weight": (16, 32),
+        "head.0.bias": (16,),
+        "head.2.weight": (2, 16),
+        "head.2.bias": (2,),
+    }
+    state = checkpoint.get("model")
+    if (
+        checkpoint.get("n_in") != width
+        or checkpoint.get("epoch") != 0
+        or not isinstance(state, dict)
+        or set(state) != set(shapes)
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint tensor map, input width or selected epoch differs from H16x1")
+    for name, shape in shapes.items():
+        tensor = state[name]
+        if (
+            tuple(tensor.shape) != shape
+            or tensor.dtype != torch.float32
+            or not torch.isfinite(tensor).all().item()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint tensor {name} has wrong shape, dtype or values")
+    if not torch.all(state["std"] > 0).item():
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint input normalization has nonpositive scales")
+    return {
+        "checkpoint_sha256": identity.fixed_file_sha256,
+        "selected_checkpoint_sha256": identity.selected_file_sha256,
+        "checkpoint_payload_sha256": identity.payload_sha256,
+        "provenance_sha256": sha(paths["provenance.json"]),
+        "history_sha256": sha(paths["history.json"]),
+        "training_state_sha256": sha(paths["training_state.pt"]),
+        "optimizer_attempts": attempts,
+        "optimizer_completed_updates": completed,
+        "amp_skipped_updates": skipped,
+        "gradient_stats_steps": grad["steps"],
+        "gradient_nonfinite_steps": grad["nonfinite_steps"],
+        "gradient_stats": grad,
+        "input_width": width,
+        "hidden": 16,
+        "layers": 1,
+    }
+
+
+def grader_call(
+    grader: Any, work: Path, run: str, split_path: Path, output: Path
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Invoke and validate one official standalone endpoint grade, with no reference."""
+    result = grader.grade_endpoint(
+        work,
+        run,
+        0,
+        split_path,
+        output,
+        reference=None,
+        n_boot=20,
+        scratch_dir=work / "scratch/grade",
+    )
+    score = result.get("endpoint", {}).get("score")
+    if (
+        not isinstance(score, dict)
+        or score.get("metric_id") != "global_wp_clip2_v1"
+        or type(score.get("selected_rows")) is not int
+        or score["selected_rows"] <= 0
+        or not math.isfinite(score.get("wp", math.nan))
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("official grader returned no finite scored-row endpoint")
+    return {
+        "result": result,
+        "score": score,
+        "signature": str(inspect.signature(grader.grade_endpoint)),
+        "arguments": {
+            "root": str(work),
+            "run": run,
+            "epoch": 0,
+            "split_path": str(split_path),
+            "reference": None,
+            "n_boot": 20,
+        },
+    }

+# PR14 causal-innovation successor review
+
+## Finding
+
+The native `a266b036b02e8e012c6eb31072291dad618a169d` implementation supports a clean, same-width, cold-start test of its innovation channels. Use the same `causal_innovations` mode in both arms and vary only `--research-feature-control`: `none` activates innovations; `newest` zeros the final 16 innovation channels. The model receives 80 appended features in both arms (64 projected slow/fast moment statistics plus 16 innovations), for a total input width of `112 raw + 99 event + 80 = 291`. This preserves the architecture, parameter layout, and total parameter count across the paired arms. The control's final 16 input columns are inactive, which is the intended feature ablation, not a separate active-capacity control.
+
+This is a **new R01-recipe successor**, not a faithful execution of historical PR14's proposed 12-epoch WSD teacher/cache experiment. Historical teacher/cache ancestry and its blocked cache-schema attempt must remain a separate record. Do not import teachers, distillation targets, caches, parent weights, or continuation state into this cold labels-only comparison.
+
+## Source path and lineage
+
+The feature path in `src/wnn/research_features.py` computes the current 16-channel projection from `x[t]`, estimates slow/fast moments causally, and standardizes each innovation against the previous slow mean and variance. It does not read labels or future rows. `fit_research_feature_prior` in `src/wnn/training/inputs.py` fits prior moments on raw inputs only, using a deterministic seed-derived sample of at most 32 source-qualified fit groups and every 64th row. For the campaign split path, the trainer passes `train_idx` plus the remaining fit-pool `extra_valid`; `CampaignSplit.assert_fit_groups` rejects the evaluation fold from both pools. Freeze and receipt the fold manifest, actual selected `(split,row_group)` membership and hash, prior arrays/hash, and dataset/source identities for every cell. Candidate/control in the same fold/seed must use the identical prior; never reuse it across folds.
+
+Training checkpoints store the mode/control in `args`, the `n_in` width, normalization buffers, the validated prior and prior provenance. `scripts/predict_run.py` restores the checkpoint's mode/control and prior before rebuilding inputs; `src/wnn/streaming.py` also has an explicit moment state and a first-row reset path. The input normalization is fitted from the fit loader and clamps standard deviations at `0.001`; consequently the masked control innovation columns remain exactly zero after normalization while all other columns follow the usual fit-only normalization. Keep the fixed epoch-5 checkpoint and evaluate it only after fitting.
+
+## Proposed command
+
+Use the exact R01 labels-only recipe, adding only the paired feature settings below. Replace placeholders per frozen fold/seed cell; the two arms share every other argument and source/data identity.
+
+```bash
+python scripts/train_rnn.py \
+  --name <unique-cell-arm-name> --hidden 512 --layers 1 \
+  --valid-fold <fold> --split-manifest <fold-split.json> --device cuda \
+  --arch gru --cell gru --enc linear --dropout 0 --train-seqs 10607 \
+  --train-source train+valid --valid-train-fraction 1 --valid-repeat 1 \
+  --n-valid-folds 4 --full-valid --eval-source vfold \
+  --batch 8 --chunk 2000 --epochs 6 \
+  --checkpoint-policy fixed --checkpoint-epoch 5 --no-eval-during-fit \
+  --seed <seed> --precision fp32 --loss wmse --loss-norm chunk \
+  --batch-order seeded --deterministic --sync-free --fused-adam --grad-stats \
+  --optim adamw --lr 0.0001 --beta2 0.999 --wd 0.01 \
+  --sched onecycle --warmup-frac 0.05 --head-lr-mult 1 --clip 1 \
+  --save-training-state \
+  --research-features causal_innovations \
+  --research-feature-control <none-or-newest>
+```
+
+Use the source's strict-FP32 runtime configuration and verify FP32 parameters, activations, optimizer state and evaluation, autocast off, TF32 off and highest float32 matmul precision in receipts. `--precision fp32` is required because the CLI defaults to FP16. For the post-fit export/prediction, select `--epoch 5` and explicitly request `--inference-precision fp32`; check exact `[groups,20000,2]` FP32 predictions and grade with the unchanged official `global_wp_clip2_v1` path. Do not use outer-fold scores during fitting or checkpoint selection.
+
+## Required gates
+
+The exact-source tests already cover synthetic prefix invariance, NumPy/Torch/streaming parity, the newest-mask width and zero suffix, trainer input assembly at width 291, `StreamingGraph` parity/reset for both controls, and an ONNX state round trip. Before admitting the CP30 fits:
+
+- Run `tests/test_causal_moment_features.py` and `tests/test_streaming_graph.py` in a Torch-enabled CPU environment. I extracted those tests and source at the exact commit; this audit environment has no Torch, so pytest collected both files but skipped them.
+- Add or run a bounded synthetic 20,000-row case that crosses both 512-row feature-scan and 2,000-row training chunk boundaries. Compare NumPy, batched Torch, chunked/row-streamed features, and the same small GRU's batch versus streaming predictions for both controls; mutate only the future suffix to confirm strict prefix invariance and run A-B-A sequence-reset checks.
+- Round-trip an epoch-5 checkpoint for each arm through the actual predictor with FP32 inference. Assert `n_in == 291`, mode/control, prior member/hash, input normalization buffers, model source hash and output shape/dtype all match the fit receipt. Independently recompute the official score from the saved prediction and verify identical evaluation row identities for each paired cell.
+- Validate each prior's selected groups against its outer split and ensure no held-out evaluation group appears in the prior or normalization fit membership. Hash the exact deployed source tree and split/data inputs; the PR body alone is not a source binding.
+
+## Comparison and limits
+
+Freeze 30 paired `(fold,seed)` cells per arm, paired on identical fold/seed, fit membership, sample order, update budget, optimizer, checkpoint and runtime. The native control estimates the incremental value of the 16 innovations conditional on the 64 moment channels; it does not test the broader historical teacher/cache recipe or prove transfer to a student/other architecture. All four folds are exposed development folds, not a pristine holdout. Predeclare a useful-effect threshold and report every endpoint, failures, per-fold paired deltas and seed/component uncertainty; do not interpret 30 fits or row count as independent markets.
+
+No scientific fits or GPU operations were run for this review. Static source inspection used commit `a266b036b02e8e012c6eb31072291dad618a169d`. Exact-source feature tests were attempted with the audit Python but skipped because Torch is not installed there.

+  "body": "# [Experiment] trajectory-average: Fixed checkpoint trajectory averaging\n\n1. **Status, lineage and ownership**\n\n   Implementation handoff / proposed comparison, not a fitted result. Lineage: **student**. IDs: `H-DRAFT-TRAJECTORY-AVERAGE-20261017`, `E-DRAFT-TRAJECTORY-AVERAGE-20261017-R1`. Author/source: team repository plus this October17 draft, based on main/research-team `18407ecfa3b02d4db70cfb3c34abbacd6653e79d`. Receiving researcher owns device adaptation, source-clean bindings, profiling and complete run/evaluation return. New code in this PR: none; reuse linked existing implementation, preserving original source.\n\n2. **Why it should work**\n\n   Averaging a fixed optimizer trajectory may improve a deterministic endpoint without extra fitting. Expect stable cross-fold endpoint gain over the same final checkpoint. The strongest general alternative is extra capacity, changed optimization or target calibration rather than the proposed mechanism; freeze the indicated matched controls. Current source evidence: Two F0seed trajectory averages constructed; export/grade pending.\n\n3. **Where more compute buys quality**\n\n   More compute buys complete fitting horizons, the30 paired cells, clean teacher cohorts and explicit capacity/context ladders; there is no measured scaling law. For student mechanisms use a single card per fit when it fits, and compare downstream official student/blend quality rather than teacher score alone. Large Transformer teachers can use multiple cards and207M/682M starting branches, with1.65B/long-context extensions conditional on evidence and memory. Do not assume all8 cards accelerate a small GRU. No leaderboard impact is measured or numerically predicted.\n\n4. **Frozen comparison and training proposal**\n\n   Arms: `fixed-final-checkpoint`, `fixed-trajectory-average`. All use FP32 parameters, activations, states, gradients and optimizer state; autocast and TF32 off, no quantization. The adjacent recipe records **starting proposals**, not a final frozen training command: AdamW, preclip norm1,12-epoch WSD with2% warmup and20% cooldown to0.1\u00d7LR. Proposed peak LR is 0.001, with parameter-group decay exclusions for biases/norms/gates to be recorded. Exact batch/accumulation/context, source-matched targets, inner checkpoint policy and successful-update count must be bound before fits. Changing the historical FP16/two-epoch recipe to this route is an explicit successor, not a faithful rerun. Scale/context/horizon sweeps are separate frozen arms, not post-result tuning hidden within these30 cells.\n\n5. **Thirty paired runs**\n\n   Each scientific arm uses F0/F1 seeds1001\u20131008 and F2/F3 seeds1001\u20131007:30 fits per arm. Candidate/control share cells and membership. Source-clean ancestors, normalizers and cache hashes must be bound independently for every fold; old F0 parents cannot simply be reused across folds. No runs in this matrix have started. `60` fits are required for all named arms; this is a plan, not a compute allocation.\n\n6. **Validation and statistical significance**\n\n   Official `global_wp_clip2_v1`, unchanged \u00b12 evaluation clipping and original clipped-label magnitude weights. Primary statistic: one quarter times each fold's mean paired endpoint WP delta, then summed; compute scores per fit, not from seed-averaged predictions. Use the [workflow's seed/component procedures](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/trajectory-average/research/unified/methods/EXPERIMENT_DRAFT_WORKFLOW_20261017_R1.md),10000 resamples, RNG17017. Separate conditional component uncertainty, fitting-seed variability, observed-fold sensitivity and unknown public transfer. Specify primary contrasts/multiplicity (Holm within frozen primary contrast family) before results. Thirty cells do not ensure power; do not treat rows, overlapping fits or four folds as many independent markets. All existing folds are exposed.\n\n7. **Future leakage and representative validation**\n\n   Inputs/feature transforms must be causal with sequence reset and fitting-only scaling. Audit source-qualified component overlap, aliases and teacher/initializer/preprocessing ancestry. True competition labels may reference future horizons; AR feedback accepts only own predictions. Check prefix invariance, reset/reload and intended chunk semantics before expensive runs. Report by source, fold, target, sequence position and activity/target-magnitude regimes; unknown anonymous clocks limit forward-market claims. No clean-validation claim is made for reused fitted groups.\n\n8. **Decision-changing outcome**\n\n   **Useful-effect threshold is deliberately pending**, to be justified from baseline variance, student transfer and GPU cost before fits. Success: a practically useful paired endpoint gain with acceptable fold/seed behavior and relevant downstream transfer. Uncertainty: an unresolved effect or heterogeneous regimes can justify a bounded targeted follow-up. Negative result: no useful gain or a concrete failure mode narrows this recipe; an interval crossing0 does not close the whole direction. Record whether the result changes teacher, student or target-link allocation. No retrospective threshold selection.\n\n9. **How to run and remaining integration**\n\n   **Not a ready-to-launch full-data B300 trainer.** Rebind fixed checkpoint epochs and normalization per fold/seed; preserve existing constructed artifacts; evaluate complete FP32 endpoints.\n\n   From the repository root, install the repository's pinned Python/Torch environment on the receiving host and record the actual CUDA/driver/Torch/container identities. Mount only permitted supplied data and source-qualified split/teacher/cache assets on physical storage. Inspect actual B300 topology and FP32 kernel support; no claimed throughput or wall time. Run the implemented **plan command**:\n\n   ```bash\n   python research/experiment_drafts/trajectory-average/run_plan.py\n   ```\n\n   This prints the30-cell matrix and missing bindings; it does **not** train. Existing implementation entry points are linked below.  \n\n   A receiving-host multi-GPU teacher launch will use `torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=<measured_count> <completed_teacher_trainer> ...`; this is a **shape of command, not an existing executable trainer**. Existing `scripts/train_rnn.py` handles GRU fitting and exposes `--precision fp32`, `--seed`, `--valid-fold`, `--split-manifest`, `--grad-stats`, `--save-training-state`; keep its cache/provenance validation. No automatic launch or queue is provided. For initializer work reuse the linked phase runner rather than pretending it accepts generic trainer flags. Resume only from matching source/config and complete optimizer/scheduler/RNG/sampler/state, otherwise restart a declared boundary.\n\n10. **Evidence and archives to return**\n\n   Explicitly hook `wnn.research_reporting.RunRecorder`; it does not instrument trainers automatically. Save source/config/ancestry/environment; attempted/completed steps, losses/components, param-group LR, preclip gradient norm, clipping/nonfinite counts, scores/masks/unit counts, timing/throughput and peak memory. Outer validation reports cannot choose checkpoints. Save all cells, failures, checkpoints/prediction manifests and an English terminal result note.\n\n   ```bash\n   python scripts/research_result_bundle.py --root <run_dir> --output-dir <archive_dir> \\\n     --evidence run_metadata.json --evidence metrics.jsonl \\\n     --evidence terminal_result.json --weight checkpoints/final.pt\n   ```\n\n   The explicit-file bundler writes separate evidence.tar and weights.tar plus SHA256 manifest; add prediction/grade/provenance files explicitly as more --evidence arguments. Keep datasets out. Return private archive locations/hashes separately from this PR, and keep the provenance manifests/narrative notes indexed in Git.\n\n11. **Results, provenance and merge trace**\n\n   No new fits or hardware checks; score/LB impact unknown. +  "body": "# [Experiment] causal-innovation: Causal innovation residuals beyond moment features\n\n1. **Status, lineage and ownership**\n\n   Implementation handoff / proposed comparison, not a fitted result. Lineage: **teacher/student**. IDs: `H-DRAFT-CAUSAL-INNOVATION-20261017`, `E-DRAFT-CAUSAL-INNOVATION-20261017-R1`. Author/source: team repository plus this October17 draft, based on main/research-team `18407ecfa3b02d4db70cfb3c34abbacd6653e79d`. Receiving researcher owns device adaptation, source-clean bindings, profiling and complete run/evaluation return. New code in this PR: none; reuse linked existing implementation, preserving original source.\n\n2. **Why it should work**\n\n   Residualizing observable changes against causal moments may expose signal obscured by levels. Expect innovation channels to add value beyond equal-width moments. The strongest general alternative is extra capacity, changed optimization or target calibration rather than the proposed mechanism; freeze the indicated matched controls. Current source evidence: Existing matched pair blocked on cache schema before fits; execution failure is not negative science.\n\n3. **Where more compute buys quality**\n\n   More compute buys complete fitting horizons, the30 paired cells, clean teacher cohorts and explicit capacity/context ladders; there is no measured scaling law. For student mechanisms use a single card per fit when it fits, and compare downstream official student/blend quality rather than teacher score alone. Large Transformer teachers can use multiple cards and207M/682M starting branches, with1.65B/long-context extensions conditional on evidence and memory. Do not assume all8 cards accelerate a small GRU. No leaderboard impact is measured or numerically predicted.\n\n4. **Frozen comparison and training proposal**\n\n   Arms: `matched-moments`, `moments-plus-innovation`. All use FP32 parameters, activations, states, gradients and optimizer state; autocast and TF32 off, no quantization. The adjacent recipe records **starting proposals**, not a final frozen training command: AdamW, preclip norm1,12-epoch WSD with2% warmup and20% cooldown to0.1\u00d7LR. Proposed peak LR is 0.001, with parameter-group decay exclusions for biases/norms/gates to be recorded. Exact batch/accumulation/context, source-matched targets, inner checkpoint policy and successful-update count must be bound before fits. Changing the historical FP16/two-epoch recipe to this route is an explicit successor, not a faithful rerun. Scale/context/horizon sweeps are separate frozen arms, not post-result tuning hidden within these30 cells.\n\n5. **Thirty paired runs**\n\n   Each scientific arm uses F0/F1 seeds1001\u20131008 and F2/F3 seeds1001\u20131007:30 fits per arm. Candidate/control share cells and membership. Source-clean ancestors, normalizers and cache hashes must be bound independently for every fold; old F0 parents cannot simply be reused across folds. No runs in this matrix have started. `60` fits are required for all named arms; this is a plan, not a compute allocation.\n\n6. **Validation and statistical significance**\n\n   Official `global_wp_clip2_v1`, unchanged \u00b12 evaluation clipping and original clipped-label magnitude weights. Primary statistic: one quarter times each fold's mean paired endpoint WP delta, then summed; compute scores per fit, not from seed-averaged predictions. Use the [workflow's seed/component procedures](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/causal-innovation/research/unified/methods/EXPERIMENT_DRAFT_WORKFLOW_20261017_R1.md),10000 resamples, RNG17017. Separate conditional component uncertainty, fitting-seed variability, observed-fold sensitivity and unknown public transfer. Specify primary contrasts/multiplicity (Holm within frozen primary contrast family) before results. Thirty cells do not ensure power; do not treat rows, overlapping fits or four folds as many independent markets. All existing folds are exposed.\n\n7. **Future leakage and representative validation**\n\n   Inputs/feature transforms must be causal with sequence reset and fitting-only scaling. Audit source-qualified component overlap, aliases and teacher/initializer/preprocessing ancestry. True competition labels may reference future horizons; AR feedback accepts only own predictions. Check prefix invariance, reset/reload and intended chunk semantics before expensive runs. Report by source, fold, target, sequence position and activity/target-magnitude regimes; unknown anonymous clocks limit forward-market claims. +  "body": "# [Experiment] E-KALMAN-LOCAL-TREND-B300-20261018: causal smoother GRU teachers and distillation\n\n## 1. Status, lineage and owner\n\nThis is an implementation and profile-preparation draft, not a completed experiment. It adds a differentiable local-trend feature module, matched EMA and zero-feature raw arms, a strict-FP32 adapter to the canonical modular trainer, adapter-aware prediction reconstruction, and adapter/provenance checks in the existing distillation-cache builder. The source base is `research-team`; the branch and final commit are recorded by the PR. Hypothesis `H-KALMAN-LOCAL-TREND-20261018`; experiment `E-KALMAN-LOCAL-TREND-B300-20261018`. No B300 profile, PyTorch smoke, task fit, student cache, task grade or performance claim has been produced. A separate NumPy synthetic receipt is preserved and labeled as such.\n\nUpdated local discovery evidence (fixed-input replay, not B300 training): the expanded panel covers 141 previously exposed F0 groups and 82 source components, after the initial 16-group screen showed +0.000338 WP. On the wider panel, raw scored 0.72188269 WP and local-trend input replacement scored 0.72199901 WP (delta +0.00011632; paired component-bootstrap 95% interval [\u22120.00007495, +0.00028789]). This is one raw-input-trained checkpoint with four inputs replaced only at inference on the same exposed fold; the wider follow-up was selected after seeing the first point. It is therefore an attenuated, uncertain discovery result with a train/inference representation mismatch, not evidence for a trained feature, student transfer, online updates, or public transfer. The retained-raw teacher/student path proposed here remains unrun.\n\nCheckpoint loading is strict for both paths: the Kalman adapter is reconstructed\nfrom checkpoint metadata and its state dict, while standard family teachers\nload their saved state dict into the canonical model before prediction export.\nThis is required for valid teacher caches; shape and finiteness checks alone\ncannot detect random initialized predictions.\n\nFor adapted checkpoints, provenance binds the hashes of both\n`src/wnn/kalman_local_trend.py` and `src/wnn/nn.py`. Prediction export checks\nthe current implementation against those training hashes before inference;\nthe sidecar records current hashes and the prediction-driver hash. Cache\nconstruction independently checks the current files against both checkpoint\nprovenance and prediction sidecar before it accepts the teacher.\n\n## 2. Why it should work\n\nA local-linear-trend filter can expose a causal estimate of level, slope and innovation uncertainty to the GRU, providing a compact inductive bias for changing latent regimes. The strongest alternative is that ordinary smoothing or the extra input projection explains any change. For both the four-channel local pilot and full 112-channel scope, the primary control is an EMA whose gain is the fixed scalar random-walk Kalman steady-state gain; the fixed-Q/R local-trend arm separates trend-state structure from learned Q/R. A scope-matched raw arm appends zeros so each four-arm set has the same GRU width and projection shape. The learned filter uses positive scalar Q/R parameters tied by state family across selected channels. All arms retain the original raw input.\n\n## 3. Compute advantage and scaling path\n\nThe competition payoff is through a better fixed-size GRU student, not a\nteacher-only score: a Kalman teacher must improve the matched four-family\nstudent-cache endpoint, then retain a useful quality/runtime/package-size\ntradeoff in the final served pipeline.\n\nThe filter adds four features per selected raw channel and a small number of learned scalars, but its eager Python time loop may erase that nominal arithmetic advantage. The 112-channel case adds 448 inputs to the H1024 projection and may be activation-memory intensive. An actual B300 profile at the full planned shape must precede scientific fitting; no time estimate is supplied. Each arm uses fresh H1024\u00d72 weights in this primary attribution experiment. A clean-parent strong-model continuation is a separate future factor: compare it against a matched fresh model and preserve identical parent ancestry across feature treatments before claiming a continuation benefit. If the teacher has value, the included path replaces one clean same-fold teacher family in the existing four-family student cache. Larger GRU teachers, teacher-only/student-only/combined feature placement, and distillation at larger context are later scaling experiments. Teacher DDP is not implemented or required for the independent small-GRU cells.\n\n## 4. Frozen comparison\n\nThe task target is the original two competition outputs under the canonical WMSE training objective; there is no next-input reconstruction target. Direct teachers use fresh H1024\u00d72 GRUs, batch 16, chunk 2,000, AdamW at 0.001, weight decay 0.01, gradient clipping 1, two epochs, OneCycle over the exact update budget, and fixed checkpoint `model_ep1`. Students use fresh H256\u00d72 GRUs, the existing two-epoch fixed-`model_ep1` cache recipe, and `--distill-alpha 0.5`. Use canonical fit-only global normalization, identical sampler/order semantics within paired cells, and sequence state reset at each source-qualified sequence while carrying state over chunks. FP32 is required for weights, inputs, recurrent/filter states, loss, gradients and optimizer; AMP, GradScaler and CUDA TF32 are disabled. The official metric may use FP64 accumulators. No per-sequence or future-row transform is added. The code and exact commands are in [recipe.json](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/kalman-teacher-gru-distill-b300/research/experiment_drafts/kalman_teacher_gru_distill_b300/recipe.json).\n\n## 5. Thirty paired runs\n\nEvery arm uses the same 30 exposed fold/seed cells: F0/F1 with seeds 1001\u20131008 and F2/F3 with seeds 1001\u20131007, for 8/8/7/7 cells. The direct teacher matrix is raw-zero-pad, steady-state EMA, fixed local trend and learned local trend at `pilot4` and `all112`; this is eight arms. The student matrix has a matched existing-cache control plus pilot4-Kalman and all112-Kalman source-replacement arms; this is three more arms. Total: 11 arms, 330 scientific fits, scheduled as 42 waves of up to eight independent fits. Launch one fit per GPU; no DDP command is supported. The same seed identities pair arms within each fold. All four folds have prior exposure; this is robustness evidence, not a pristine holdout. `pilot4` is the local screening scope, while `all112` is the expanded channel-scope comparison. Profile the all112 learned arm before fit admission; if the profile passes, run both predeclared matrices in full. Pilot quality does not gate all112 inclusion.\n\n## 6. Validation and significance\n\nFor seed variability, use NumPy PCG64 seed `20261018` for 10,000\npercentile-bootstrap replicates: draw eight seed identities with replacement\nfrom 1001\u20131008, apply the same multiplicities in every fold, renormalize over\neach fold's available seeds, and redraw if any fold has zero available\nmultiplicity. For evaluation-unit variability, use separate PCG64 seed\n`20261019` for 10,000 paired source-component bootstrap replicates within each\nfold, sharing component multiplicities across arms and seed cells. Report the\ntwo marginal 95% intervals separately; both condition on the exposed folds and\nfixed fitted endpoints.\n\nGrade with unchanged `global_wp_clip2_v1`, fixed scored rows and its original clipping and weighting. Primary contrasts are learned versus EMA and learned versus fixed local trend separately for both scopes (four tests). Secondary contrasts are learned versus same-scope raw-zero-pad control and each Kalman-family student versus the shared matched-cache student (four tests). If all are reported, apply Holm correction across all eight. Use the equal-fold mean of paired seed means, a 10,000-replicate crossed seed-identity bootstrap with shared seed multiplicities across folds, and a separate 10,000-replicate paired source-component bootstrap within each fold. Report fold and seed variation separately; intervals condition on exposed folds and fitted endpoints. Profiles, synthetic checks and PyTorch parity checks are engineering evidence, not quality comparisons.\n\n## 7. Leakage and coverage\n\nThe canonical raw/event input width is 211; the adapter rejects alternative feature assembly. The four pilot channels `[0,3,52,55]` are anonymous indices and carry no physical interpretation; pilot-only findings do not extrapolate to 112 channels. The `all112` scope is explicitly separate. All features are causal and state resets by sequence. Canonical input normalization is fitted from the exact training-view loader and reused from checkpoint statistics at inference. No targets enter feature construction. Before cache building, freeze the four teacher family run IDs, epochs, split hashes, coefficients and checkpoint hashes per cell. The existing builder checks clean-fold fit membership, prediction sidecars, row ordering and checkpoint bytes. For treatment caches only `samefold_baseline` is replaced, at its unchanged coefficient. Shared ancestors are not independent replications. Previously exposed folds remain exposed.\n\n## 8. Decision-changing result\n\nA mean gain around `+0.0005` weighted Pearson is a provisional reference for prioritizing a follow-up, not a kill threshold. A useful result also needs compatible behavior across folds and acceptable measured resource cost. A zero-crossing interval is inconclusive. Negative results apply to the tested state family, channel scope, schedule and teacher/student path, not all Kalman or smoothing mechanisms. If the local pilot differs from full112, report the interaction as channel-scope dependence rather than treating the smaller result as confirmation. Continue with a clean-parent warm-start/fresh factorial, larger teacher, or student feature placement only when the profile and evidence justify it.\n\n## 9. How to run\n\nUse the exact branch source with the compatible project environment. `WNN_PROJECT_ROOT` must be a writable project namespace containing supplied `train.parquet`/`valid.parquet`, target indexes, source-qualified fold manifests, run outputs and caches. Mount the code checkout read-only at the exact source SHA. Place cache, predictions, logs and checkpoints on physical worker storage, not `/tmp` or `/dev/shm`. Run the full112 H1024 profile gate on the actual eight-B300 host and record driver/runtime versions, host/GPU peak memory, finite optimizer-update latency, filter/GRU forward-backward throughput and input overhead. If resized, freeze the new dimensions/batch and reprofile every direct arm at both scopes before admission. The packet has a synthetic smoke command, teacher training command, prediction export commands, cache builder command and standard student command in [README](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/kalman-teacher-gru-distill-b300/research/experiment_drafts/kalman_teacher_gru_distill_b300/README.md) and [recipe](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/kalman-teacher-gru-distill-b300/research/experiment_drafts/kalman_teacher_gru_distill_b300/recipe.json). The smoke and every fit remain unrun. Use one independent process per GPU; no torchrun/DDP route is implemented. Student fits are blocked pending a clean per-cell four-family registry.\n\n## 10. Evidence to return\n\nFor each optimizer update preserve attempted/successful steps, progress, loss, LR, preclip gradient norm and clipping/nonfinite counts. Each cell must bind branch/source/config hashes, software/hardware identity, split and membership hashes, teacher ancestry, optimizer-update budget, checkpoint/prediction hashes, official score, paired deltas, phase times and peak host/GPU memory. Archive evidence and model weights separately, including file and archive SHA256 and private storage location in the run manifest. Retain every valid cell and negative/inconclusive result. The local NumPy synthetic receipt and source are included in `evidence/`; the receipt reports 841,376 KiB peak RSS, so requested support-resource verification is unconfirmed. It contains no task data, labels or task model result.\n\n## 11. Results and trace\n\nNo task cell has been admitted or run from this branch; teacher/student quality and B300 runtime are unknown. A source-only independent review initially found that the adapted-source sidecar echoed checkpoint metadata rather than validating current filter code and omitted the imported GRU core. The follow-up fix binds both source files through training provenance, prediction export and cache construction; the independent source-only review cleared that path. The [review summary](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/main/research/unified/reviews/KALMAN_B300_DRAFT_REVIEW_20261018_R1.md) is indexed in the main checkout. The local fixed-GRU screen is separately recorded in the [Kalman results note](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/main/research/campaign_2026-10-18/online_features_r1/kalman_filter_probe/RESULTS_R2.md) and does not establish trained-feature value.\n\nThe three source records are [Backprop KF](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.07148), [KalmanNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.10043) and the [AI-Aided Kalman Filters survey/tutorial](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12289). These motivate differentiable and hybrid filtering as a direction; they do not establish a Challenge2 gain. The full112 actual B300 profile and per-cell clean teacher registry are still required before fitting. This PR is an implementation handoff, not fit authorization; no public score, leaderboard transfer, speedup or competitive result is claimed.\n\n### Related local recurrent-state screen (18 October 2026)\n\nA separate matched local screen retained raw inputs and appended 39 causal groupwise fast/slow Kalman innovation-energy states. The active arm scored **0.67986413 WP**, versus **0.67981250** for an equal-width zero-state control (delta **+0.00005163**). A paired bootstrap over 141 exposed F0 components gave conditional 95% interval **[-0.00013143, +0.00027018]**; position-bin effects were mixed. Both arms used the same trained parent, 32-component fitting subset, seed/order, normalization, and 210 FP32 updates. This is one exposed fold and one incremental fine-tune, not a seed/fold replication, clean validation result, student-cache result, or evidence of long-horizon online adaptation.\n\nThis is adjacent evidence for the broader retained-raw Kalman feature question, not a replication or ranking of the local-trend teacher/student arms described above. The local packet and receipts are currently in the main worktree at `research/campaign_2026-10-18/online_features_r1/kalman_recurrent_groupfast_slow_r1/`; they are not attached to this PR branch. No separate B300 draft is justified by this near-zero result.\n",
